title: Stacks lemma for a reduced closed subcurve of a nodal curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $X$ be a reduced finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Suppose that at every closed point $x$ where $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is not smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is finite separable over $k$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and its completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is, as a $k$-algebra, $\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(uv)$ (maximal-ideal-adic completion and two-variable formal power series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]). If $Y\subset X$ is a reduced closed subscheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] equidimensional of dimension $1$, then (1) at every nonsmooth closed point $y$ of $Y$ its residue field is finite separable over $k$ and its completed local ring is $\kappa(y)[[u,v]]/(uv)$; and (2) if $Z\subset X$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus Y$ (the smallest closed subscheme through which the open immersion factors), then (a) the scheme-theoretic intersection $Y\cap Z$ is a finite disjoint union of spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of finite separable extensions of $k$, (b) every point of $Y\cap Z$ is a nonsmooth node of $X$ with completed local ring $\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(uv)$, and (c) $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth at every point of $Y\cap Z$.

proof.text: Finite type gives Noetherianity and the Jacobson property. Apply complementary-pure-subcurve-boundary-finite to obtain finite and discrete T and closed ambient boundary points.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: Apply split-nodal-subcurve-local-dichotomy at each closed point of Y. The second alternative is smooth on Y, so any nonsmooth Y point is in the stalk-isomorphism alternative. Transfer finiteness and separability through the canonical residue-field isomorphism and transfer the nodal completion through split-node-completion-transport. The germ-stalk-map identity proves compatibility of the transported scalar maps.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: For t in T the first alternative of the local dichotomy is impossible: the pullback condition places the ambient image in the complementary closure. Thus X is nonsmooth there, Y is smooth, and the T stalk is a field. The original nodal hypothesis supplies precisely the required ambient completion, with its scalar identity.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: All boundary stalks are fields, hence T is reduced. The composite closed immersion T→X induces residue-field isomorphisms; therefore the finite separable ambient residue fields give finite separable residue fields for T. Apply finite-reduced-discrete-residue-fields to obtain the coproduct and its equations over Spec k.

I read the item in full, the parent's two steps that apply it, and every cited node's statement. The item is a split-node specialization of 0E38 with the same conclusions (1) and (2)(a)-(c), and it matches how the parent uses it. There are no new nodes and no cycle (I checked the transitive closure of the cited nodes, 556 of them). The source's typo O_{Y,Y} is not reproduced.

Checks by step: Step 1, the component-union node and the reduced scheme-theoretic closure, with all points of T closed in X. Step 2, smooth gives regular gives domain, so a single component passes through y. Step 3, using faithful flatness and surjectivity on Spec, the primes of F[[u,v]]/(uv) are exactly (u), (v), (u,v), so at most two minimal primes. Steps 5-6, the completion of A/p_i is C/p_iC, reduced of dimension 1; radicality, contraction and (u)∩(v)=0 force p_1C=(v) and p_2C=(u), and p_1+p_2=m. Step 7, 07NY and 00TV. Step 9, 0AAX gives a finite discrete T made of copies of Spec F. Small cases checked: Y empty, Y=X, one axis of uv=0 over F, both axes kept, an irreducible nodal curve, and a nontrivial finite separable F/k. I accept all ten declared tool_uses.

Fixes, all in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/lem-trf-stacks-nodal-closed-subcurve.json: (1) Step 7 now proves that a finite separable algebraic F/k is separable in the sense of def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension, which the 00TV node requires, and cites that definition in uses and proof_deps. (2) Step 1 now gives the sobriety argument for dim T<=0. (3) Step 2 now spells out how the components through y correspond to the minimal primes of the local ring, through an affine open and localization. The statement and every other field are unchanged.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
